emergencyNumber: No reliable centralized emergency number. Contact your embassy or organization directly.
healthcareSystem: Healthcare system is severely degraded by ongoing conflict. Juba Teaching Hospital is the main facility but has extreme shortages. NGO-run clinics (MSF, ICRC) provide much of the functional healthcare. Outside Juba, healthcare is virtually nonexistent. Evacuation is essential for any serious condition.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is among the lowest in the world. Facilities lack basic supplies, reliable electricity, and qualified staff. English is the official language but many healthcare workers speak Arabic or local languages. All serious medical conditions require evacuation to Nairobi, Kenya.
pharmacyHours: A few pharmacies in Juba open irregularly, approximately 8am-5pm. No reliable pharmacy access outside Juba.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacy access is extremely limited. Counterfeit and expired medications are a major concern. Bring ALL medications you could possibly need. NGO workers should ensure their organization provides medical supplies. English and Arabic may be spoken.
prescriptionRules: No meaningful prescription enforcement system exists. The challenge is finding any medication at all. Bring all needed medications with documentation.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging. Security forces may inspect medications at checkpoints.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry comprehensive documentation. Authorities may question any medications.

bringDocumentation: Carry extensive documentation for all medications in English and Arabic. Keep everything in original packaging. Bring far more than you think you will need — resupply is nearly impossible. Include a medical kit with first aid supplies.

travelInsurance.tips: Comprehensive travel insurance with emergency medical evacuation is absolutely essential. Many standard policies exclude South Sudan as a conflict zone — verify your policy explicitly covers it. Evacuation to Nairobi costs $20,000-80,000+. Consider specialized conflict-zone insurance providers.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is required. Malaria is endemic and prophylaxis is essential. Cholera outbreaks are common. Meningitis risk in dry season. Ensure all routine vaccinations are up to date.

waterNotes: Water is unsafe everywhere in South Sudan. Use only bottled or thoroughly treated water. Avoid ice. Water purification tablets or filters are essential. Even in Juba hotels, verify water safety. Waterborne diseases including cholera are common.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid all raw vegetables, salads, and unpeeled fruits. Street food carries high risk. UN and NGO compounds often have the safest food preparation. Bring emergency food supplies for travel outside Juba.
medicalTourismNote: South Sudan is not a medical tourism destination. The country has one of the weakest healthcare systems in the world. All specialist care requires evacuation to Nairobi, Kenya or Kampala, Uganda.
metaDescription: Health guide for South Sudan: emergency contacts, medication advice, vaccinations, water safety, and evacuation to Nairobi.

hospitals.name: Juba Teaching Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main government hospital. Extremely basic facilities with chronic shortages. English and Arabic spoken. Use only as last resort — evacuation is preferred.

hospitals.name: UNMISS Level II Hospital
hospitals.notes: UN peacekeeping hospital. Access restricted to UN personnel but may assist in extreme emergencies. Best-equipped facility in the country.

dentalCare.availability: Extremely limited. Only the most basic dental care may be available in Juba.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is virtually nonexistent. The few dentists practice in Juba with very basic equipment.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, seek help at Juba Teaching Hospital. Evacuation to Nairobi is recommended for anything beyond basic extraction.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No mental health crisis line exists
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: No civilian English-speaking therapists. Some NGOs provide trauma counseling.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are virtually nonexistent for visitors. Some NGO workers have access to organizational mental health support. Consider telehealth services if internet connectivity allows.

accessibilityInfo.overview: No accessibility infrastructure exists in South Sudan.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospitals are not accessible for wheelchair users.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible transport. Roads are unpaved and impassable in rainy season.
accessibilityInfo.tips: South Sudan is extremely challenging for travelers with mobility limitations. Infrastructure is minimal even for able-bodied travelers. Travel with an organized group and assess whether the environment can support your needs.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Extremely limited COVID testing. Some availability in Juba.
covidStatus.notes: COVID treatment capacity is negligible. Serious respiratory illness requires evacuation.

insuranceClaimProcess: Obtain whatever receipts are available. Most facilities expect cash payment. Documentation standards are poor. Contact your insurance assistance line immediately for any significant medical issue. Evacuation authorization should be arranged as quickly as possible.

commonCosts.note: Costs are low but reflect extremely basic care. USD is widely preferred. NGO clinics may provide free or subsidized care.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is essential for any serious condition. AMREF Flying Doctors provides air ambulance services in East Africa. Security conditions may delay evacuation. Ensure your evacuation provider has experience operating in conflict zones.

drugNameMap.note: Most commonly found medication, but verify expiration dates and authenticity
Unlikely to be available. Bring from home.
